notes.3: Many candidates did not realise that the acceleration of free fall is constant if friction can be ignored. Many candidates thought that the acceleration would increase.
notes.7: Many candidates showed little understanding of the concept of the principle of equilibrium. They did not understand that if an object is moving in the straight line at constant speed the resultant force on the object is zero. Most candidates thought that there must be a force in the direction of the movement.
notes.10: Although many candidates were able to identify the advantages and disadvantages of using wind turbines to generate electricity, a significant number incorrectly thought that they produced a constant output irrespective of weather conditions.
notes.12: Only stronger candidates showed an understanding of the operation of a simple barometer. Most thought that the height of the mercury column would halve if the diameter of the tube was doubled.
notes.13: Although many candidates were able to apply the formula P = , a significant number multiplied the force by the area.
notes.17: Only stronger candidates showed an understanding of thermal capacity. Most thought that the larger the temperature rise, the greater the heat capacity.
notes.18: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly and showed an understanding of the graph.
notes.22: Although most candidates chose the correct answer, many thought option D was the correct response. This showed a failure to fully understand that the direction of travel of the wave is perpendicular to the wavefronts.
notes.25: Only stronger candidates recognised that the sound travelled to the cliff, and then reflected from the cliff and travelled back to the ship. Thus, the distance from the ship to the cliff is half the total distance travelled by the sound and is equal to the speed of the sound multiplied by half the time taken, not the total time.
notes.32: Many candidates confused the circuit with a parallel circuit. Only stronger candidates recognised that in this series circuit, the current is the same all the way round the circuit.
notes.37: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly and the most common response was D (circuit R only). Many candidates did not read the question with sufficient care and thought it was asking for the circuits which produced a force on the wire in the same direction as in the original example, not the opposite direction.
notes.general_comments:
Candidates answered Questions 1, 2, 5, 8, 15, 27, 30, 35 and 38 very well. Questions 3, 7, 12, 17, 18, 25
and 37 were more challenging for many candidates.
